title: Identify the installed wallet and the right documentation release
outcome: You know exactly which build you are running and which parts of this site describe it.
completionCriterion: You can state your wallet version and know whether this site's pages describe it.
recovery: Nothing in this journey changes your wallet. Closing the page at any point loses nothing.

steps.title: Open the wallet and its settings
steps.goal: Reach the wallet's About or Settings area, where the version is shown.
steps.expected: The wallet opens. Settings lists backup status, security, and About entries.
steps.action: Click the wallet icon, then open Settings.
steps.checkpoint: You can see the settings list. If the wallet asks for a password, that is the unlock screen, not settings; unlock first.
steps.failure: If no wallet icon exists in the browser, the extension is not installed. That is a different journey.

steps.title: Read the version number
steps.goal: Find the exact version string.
steps.expected: A version like 1.0.13 or 1.7.5.8 is displayed.
steps.action: Open About (or the version row) and note the number.
steps.checkpoint: You wrote down the exact version, not a date or a build channel.
steps.failure: Some builds show the version only in the extension's detail page (browser extensions page). Both numbers are the same.

branches.note: Version 1.0.13 is the published store build from April 2025. Screens on this site may not exist in it.

steps.title: Or use Detect my wallet
steps.goal: Let this site read the version for you without you touching settings.
steps.expected: The header control reports the detected version, or says none was found.
steps.action: Click 'Detect my wallet' in this site's header. Only the version is read.
steps.checkpoint: The control names exactly what was detected and never asks for accounts or addresses.
steps.failure: An unknown version is labeled unknown. This site never guesses the nearest release.

title: Install and verify the authentic extension
outcome: The wallet is installed from a real source and you know how to check it.
completionCriterion: The extension is installed from the Chrome Web Store listing and its version is known.
recovery: An extension can be removed in the browser's extensions page at any time. Installation changes nothing on chain.

steps.title: Open the official store listing
steps.goal: Install from the publisher's listing, not a copy.
steps.expected: The Chrome Web Store opens on the Universe Wallet listing.
steps.action: Use the install link from this site's install page or the official site. Check the publisher name.
steps.checkpoint: The publisher and item identifier match the official site. Fake wallets live on near-identical URLs.
steps.failure: A listing with a different publisher, or any direct ZIP from chat or search ads, is the classic phishing pattern.

steps.title: Add the extension
steps.goal: Complete the browser install.
steps.expected: The browser asks to confirm adding the extension.
steps.action: Confirm. Pin the icon if you want it visible.
steps.checkpoint: Only the permissions the browser shows should appear. Nothing here should ask for your recovery phrase.
steps.failure: No real wallet ever asks for existing recovery words during install. A page that does is an impostor.

steps.title: Verify what you installed
steps.goal: Know the version you actually have.
steps.expected: The wallet opens on its welcome or unlock screen.
steps.action: Open settings and read the version, or use Detect my wallet here.
steps.checkpoint: You know the version and which parts of this site describe it.
steps.failure: If the wallet fails to open, remove it and reinstall from the listing; do not hunt for the missing wallet on search engines.

title: Choose between creating and importing
outcome: You know which onboarding path matches your situation before any key exists.
completionCriterion: You can say which path applies to you and why.
recovery: Choosing wrong here costs nothing; neither path creates anything until you complete it.

steps.title: Meet the welcome screen
steps.goal: See the two paths.
steps.expected: The welcome screen offers creating a new wallet or importing one.
steps.action: Read both options. Do not decide from habit.
steps.checkpoint: You know whether you have ever held recovery material for a Universe-compatible wallet before.
steps.failure: Importing a phrase you also use in another active wallet splits custody between devices. Plan for one home per phrase.

steps.title: Decide
steps.goal: Pick the honest path.
steps.expected: Clear next screen for the chosen path.
steps.action: New keys: create. Existing keys: import.
steps.checkpoint: Create for a fresh start; import only for phrase you already control and have secured.
steps.failure: Restoring from a phrase you never wrote down yourself (for example one someone gave you) hands them your money.

title: Create a wallet and secure its recovery material
outcome: A new wallet exists, its recovery phrase is backed up offline, and the backup status says so.
prerequisites: A private space where no camera can see your screen
completionCriterion: Settings shows the wallet backed up, and the phrase exists only offline in your keeping.
recovery: Until you send funds in, everything here is re-doable. Lose the phrase after funding and the money is gone; there is no reset.

steps.title: Create the device password
steps.goal: Set the password that unlocks this wallet on this device.
steps.expected: Two password fields and a Continue control.
steps.action: Enter a strong password twice and continue.
steps.checkpoint: You understand this password unlocks this device only. It is not the recovery phrase and cannot restore funds.
steps.failure: A forgotten password with no phrase means reinstalling from scratch. The phrase is the real key.

steps.title: Choose the address type
steps.goal: Pick the address model for the wallet.
steps.expected: A list of address type cards; Continue stays disabled until a scan finishes.
steps.action: Keep the default unless you have a specific reason. Continue.
steps.checkpoint: The default covers most users. Changing it later means recovery procedures.
steps.failure: Importing into a mismatched address type makes balances appear missing. They are on the other path.

steps.title: Write the recovery phrase offline
steps.goal: Capture the 12 words where no camera or clipboard can reach them.
steps.expected: The phrase is shown once, masked by secure input.
steps.action: Write the words on paper in order. Verify by re-entering when asked.
steps.checkpoint: Words exist on paper only. Never photographed, never typed into anything networked, never clipped.
steps.failure: A phrase that touched a phone camera, cloud note, or password manager sync is a leaked key waiting to be used.

steps.title: Confirm backup status
steps.goal: The wallet records that the backup step is done.
steps.expected: Home shows the wallet; Settings shows backup status.
steps.action: Open Settings and confirm the backup entry reflects your paper copy.
steps.checkpoint: Settings is the source of truth for backup state inside the wallet.
steps.failure: Dismissing the backup reminder without writing the phrase is the most common permanent-loss story.

title: Import a wallet safely
outcome: Existing keys are restored into this wallet without the phrase touching anything networked.
prerequisites: Your recovery phrase or private key, already written down
completionCriterion: The restored wallet shows the expected account and balances (or an empty account for a fresh phrase).
recovery: Import copies; it does not move. The original phrase keeps working and must stay protected.

steps.title: Choose the import source
steps.goal: Select where the keys come from.
steps.expected: A list of sources as selectable cards.
steps.action: Pick the source matching your phrase (for example a 12-word Universe-compatible wallet).
steps.checkpoint: The source card names the wallet family the phrase belongs to.
steps.failure: Wrong source means empty balances. Nothing is lost; redo with the right source.

steps.title: Enter the phrase
steps.goal: Restore keys from your offline copy.
steps.expected: A grid of twelve masked inputs.
steps.action: Type words from paper. Keep secure input on.
steps.checkpoint: The words came from paper, not from a file, a photo, or a message someone sent you.
steps.failure: A phrase someone gave you 'to import' is their lever on your money. Import only phrases you generated.

steps.title: Verify what was restored
steps.goal: Confirm the account and address type match your old wallet.
steps.expected: Home shows the restored account.
steps.action: Check the receive address against the old wallet's address where possible.
steps.checkpoint: Address type mismatch is the usual cause of 'my funds are gone' after import. They are on another derivation path.
steps.failure: If balances look missing, stop sending. Recheck the address type before anything else.

title: Receive funds for the first time
outcome: You requested your first payment to an address you verified in your own wallet.
completionCriterion: The payment appears in activity with its confirmation state.
recovery: Receiving is reversible by simply sending onward. Nothing broadcast here spends your funds.

steps.title: Open Receive
steps.goal: Get your receiving address.
steps.expected: The receive screen reports it is ready to receive.
steps.action: Open Receive from home.
steps.checkpoint: The network shown in the header matches the network the payer expects. Testnet coins and mainnet coins are not interchangeable.
steps.failure: Sending mainnet funds to a testnet address loses them. Read the network label.

steps.title: Share the address
steps.goal: Give the payer your address or QR.
steps.expected: An address string and a QR code.
steps.action: Copy, or show the QR, or request via a payment name if configured.
steps.checkpoint: Paste-back check: paste the address where you will send it to yourself and compare the first and last 6 characters.
steps.failure: Clipboard malware swaps addresses. The paste-back check defeats the common ones.

steps.title: Watch it arrive
steps.goal: See the payment and its confirmation state.
steps.expected: Activity lists the incoming payment; confirmations count up.
steps.action: Open Activity. Nothing else to do.
steps.checkpoint: A payment is spendable per the wallet's confirmation policy; large payments deserve more confirmations before you ship goods.
steps.failure: If nothing appears, verify the address the payer actually used. A wrong network or old address is the usual cause.

title: Send funds safely
outcome: You know how a safe send flows, and whether your build can send at all.
completionCriterion: Either the send completed with a transaction id, or your build showed the unavailable state because its release authorizes no sending.
recovery: Before approval, a send is fully reversible: close the screen. After broadcast, nothing can pull a transaction back.

steps.title: Check that this build can send
steps.goal: Know the send availability for your release.
steps.expected: Builds whose release authorizes no sending show a plain unavailable panel: 'This build cannot send'.
steps.action: Open the send screen and read what it actually offers.
steps.checkpoint: An unavailable state is the wallet protecting you. It is not a bug and not a network outage.
steps.failure: Nothing to fear here: an unauthorized build cannot send, cannot be talked into sending, and loses nothing.

branches.note: This source tree authorizes no sending operation. The journey stops at the unavailable state for this release; the remaining steps describe the authorized flow for when a release ships it.

steps.title: Compose the payment
steps.goal: Address, amount, fee.
steps.expected: The send form with a fee selector.
steps.action: Paste the address, set the amount, choose a fee.
steps.checkpoint: Paste-back the address. Compare fee rate to the wallet's recommendation.
steps.failure: A fee far above recommendation is a signal to stop and reread every field.

steps.title: Read the review screen like a contract
steps.goal: Approve exactly what you decided.
steps.expected: The transaction review: recipient, amount, fee, change.
steps.action: Read every output. The change output must return to your wallet.
steps.checkpoint: Every output accounted for: payment + change + fee = total.
steps.failure: Approving a screen you did not read is how every send scam works. No exception.

steps.title: Approve and track
steps.goal: Broadcast and watch for the transaction id.
steps.expected: A confirmation, then the transaction id in activity.
steps.action: Approve. Open activity to watch confirmations.
steps.checkpoint: The txid in your activity is the receipt. Confirmations mean settlement.
steps.failure: After broadcast there is no undo. A stuck transaction is bumped or dropped by its fee, not by support.

title: Understand available, unavailable, and protected balance
outcome: You can explain why the wallet may show more wealth than spendable funds.
completionCriterion: You can read the balance anatomy on home and protected outputs without surprise.

steps.title: Read the home balance anatomy
steps.goal: See total, available, and held-back amounts with the ownership line.
steps.expected: Home splits the balance when parts are not spendable.
steps.action: Compare total and available. The difference is explained below the numbers.
steps.checkpoint: Unconfirmed incoming payments and protected outputs both reduce available funds.
steps.failure: Treating the total as spendable leads to stuck payments, not losses.

steps.title: Open protected outputs
steps.goal: See what the wallet holds back and why.
steps.expected: The protected outputs screen lists held outputs with reasons.
steps.action: Open it from settings or home.
steps.checkpoint: Protected outputs carry artifacts (inscriptions, rare sats) that plain spending would destroy or move.
steps.failure: Forcing a spend that consumes a protected output can send your art with your payment.

title: Connect to a site and review requested access
outcome: You can connect a site deliberately and read what the connection actually grants.
prerequisites: A site you have decided to trust
completionCriterion: The site shows as connected in the wallet, and you can name what it may and may not do.
recovery: Disconnecting ends access instantly. Connections grant identity visibility, never spending on their own.

steps.title: Start the connection from the site
steps.goal: Trigger the wallet's connection approval.
steps.expected: The wallet opens an approval naming the site's origin.
steps.action: Click the site's Connect button.
steps.checkpoint: Read the origin in the approval. example-site.test-style names or look-alike domains mean close it.
steps.failure: Connecting on a phishing page exposes your account identity to attackers, who then tailor the scam.

steps.title: Read the request
steps.goal: Know what access is asked.
steps.expected: The approval states the account access requested.
steps.action: Approve or reject.
steps.checkpoint: A connection shows your account to the site. It does not authorize spending; signatures are separate approvals.
steps.failure: Approving unknown origins trains you to click through approvals, which is the habit scams harvest.

steps.title: Know the unverified-origin gate
steps.goal: Recognize the state the wallet shows when it cannot verify a site.
steps.expected: A full gate: 'Unable to verify this site', with no approve control.
steps.action: Nothing to click. Close it.
steps.checkpoint: The gate appears when the wallet's site check cannot complete. It fails closed on purpose.
steps.failure: No third party can legitimately 'unlock' this gate. Instructions claiming to are the scam.

title: Review a transaction or PSBT before signing
outcome: You can read a transaction review or PSBT screen and sign only what you verified.
completionCriterion: You can name what a signature commits to before any approval.
recovery: Refusing is always available and always safe. No signature, no consequence.

steps.title: Know your build's signing availability
steps.goal: Know whether this release signs at all.
steps.expected: This source tree authorizes no signing operation; provider calls refuse before any approval.
steps.action: Check the capability status for your release.
steps.checkpoint: A refusal is the gate, not an error to work around.
steps.failure: Workarounds 'to unlock signing' are always scams.

branches.note: No signing operation is authorized in this source tree, so the approval-walk steps are educational until a release ships them.

steps.title: Read the transaction anatomy
steps.goal: Inputs, outputs, fee, change: know what each means.
steps.expected: The review shows money in, money out, the fee, and change returning to you.
steps.action: Study the anatomy in the Safety Lab before you meet it live.
steps.checkpoint: You can say which outputs are yours and which leave, for any transaction shown.
steps.failure: The largest output not going to you is the classic theft shape.

steps.title: Sign or decline
steps.goal: Commit only to what you read.
steps.expected: Approval signs exactly the displayed transaction.
steps.action: Approve if every line checks; decline otherwise.
steps.checkpoint: Declining costs nothing, ever.
steps.failure: Signing unreadable data (length warnings) commits you to something you never saw.

title: Switch chain or network safely
outcome: You can move the wallet between chains and test networks without losing track of where money applies.
completionCriterion: You switched the active chain deliberately and can switch back.
recovery: Switching back restores the previous view. No funds move when you switch.

steps.title: Read the current chain
steps.goal: Know where you are before moving.
steps.expected: The header names the active chain and network.
steps.action: Check the header.
steps.checkpoint: Mainnet is real money. Test networks are for practice.
steps.failure: Doing mainnet actions on reflex after practicing on testnet is the common accident.

steps.title: Approve a switch request
steps.goal: Move deliberately when a site or you requests a chain change.
steps.expected: The approval names both the current and the target chain.
steps.action: Approve only if the target chain makes sense for what you are doing.
steps.checkpoint: After switching, every balance view is per-chain; the old chain's funds did not vanish.
steps.failure: Sites requesting switches to obscure chains are setting up a look-alike-token trick.

title: Inspect transaction history and confirmation state
outcome: You can read your activity list and know what 'confirmed' means before you rely on a payment.
completionCriterion: You can find a transaction's confirmation count and state what it implies.

steps.title: Open activity
steps.goal: See the list.
steps.expected: Transactions with direction, amount, and state. Offline builds show an explicit load failure with retry.
steps.action: Open Activity.
steps.checkpoint: An offline error with a retry control is the honest state; an always-empty list would be a lie.
steps.failure: Loading failures resolve when connectivity returns. Retry, do not re-import.

steps.title: Read confirmation state
steps.goal: Know how settled a payment is.
steps.expected: Each transaction shows its confirmations (or pending).
steps.action: Open a transaction and read its state.
steps.checkpoint: Pending means reversible by the sender; confirmed means it is in the chain and settling.
steps.failure: Shipping goods for a pending payment is trusting an unconfirmed promise.

title: Respond to a suspected compromised wallet
outcome: You contained the incident and moved remaining funds to fresh keys in the right order.
completionCriterion: Any remaining funds live under a new phrase that no suspect device or person has seen.
recovery: Speed matters more than neatness. You can clean up after the money is safe.

steps.title: Stop using the suspect wallet
steps.goal: Prevent further exposure.
steps.expected: Nothing new is signed or approved.
steps.action: Stop. Do not sign anything more, do not 'test' the wallet with small sends to check it.
steps.checkpoint: You accept that anything the suspect device can see may already be known.
steps.failure: The 'send a small test amount' reflex from compromised devices funds the attacker.

steps.title: Prepare fresh keys on a clean device
steps.goal: Create a new wallet where the compromise cannot see it.
steps.expected: A new phrase exists on paper, created on a device you trust.
steps.action: Install the wallet on a clean device or profile and create a new wallet.
steps.checkpoint: The new phrase never touches the suspect device in any form: no photo, no note, no cloud.
steps.failure: Moving funds to keys the suspect device generated (or its clipboard saw) is not an escape.

steps.title: Move funds to the new wallet
steps.goal: Transfer remaining value to fresh keys.
steps.expected: Sends complete from the old wallet to the new address.
steps.action: Send everything worth keeping. Artifacts too: a moved inscription leaves the compromised keys.
steps.checkpoint: Balance shows zero (or the amount you chose to abandon) on the old wallet.
steps.failure: Leaving 'just the cheap artifacts' leaves a trail and a hook for follow-up scams.

branches.note: If your build authorizes no sending, sweeping from it is impossible by design: use another wallet you control that holds the same keys, or accept the exposure and treat all funds as at risk.

steps.title: Retire the old phrase
steps.goal: Make sure the old keys are never funded again.
steps.expected: The old phrase is out of circulation.
steps.action: Remove the wallet from the suspect device. Mark the paper phrase as burned.
steps.checkpoint: No service, subscription, or payment card still points at the old address.
steps.failure: Reusing a leaked phrase 'one more time' is how round-two losses happen.

title: Complete a first developer connection using the simulated provider
outcome: A working integration path: detect, connect, read capabilities, handle rejection - all against the simulated provider, with a downloadable starter.
completionCriterion: Your code detects the provider, handles connection and rejection, and renders unavailable states from capabilities.
recovery: Simulation only; no wallet is touched, nothing to recover.

steps.title: Detect the provider
steps.goal: Find the wallet's injected namespace.
steps.expected: Provider aliases are known: universe, tapwallet, and variants.
steps.action: Check for window.universe in the Integration Studio doctor or your code.
steps.checkpoint: Detection says nothing about connection. It only found a candidate provider.
steps.failure: Assuming detection implies consent leads to connecting without asking.

steps.title: Simulate connect and rejection
steps.goal: See both outcomes.
steps.expected: The studio's fake provider answers requestAccounts with a simulated account, or a rejection.
steps.action: Run requestAccounts in the success and rejection scenarios.
steps.checkpoint: Rejection is a normal state your UI must render, not an exception to swallow.
steps.failure: Auto-retrying connection prompts train users to approve blindly.

steps.title: Read capabilities and render unavailable states
steps.goal: Gate every feature on what the wallet reports.
steps.expected: getCapabilities reports this release authorizes no protocol operations.
steps.action: Call getCapabilities in the simulation and render the unavailable branch.
steps.checkpoint: Your UI shows the unavailable state as a first-class outcome, not a disabled button.
steps.failure: Promising a send the wallet refuses is a broken product and a support fire.

steps.title: Download the starter and keep the loop
steps.goal: Leave with runnable code.
steps.expected: A minimal starter reflecting the contract.
steps.action: Download it from the studio and wire it into your app.
steps.checkpoint: The starter runs without any wallet installed.
steps.failure: Testing only against a real wallet hides the refusal paths your users will meet.

title: Save the emergency handbook for offline use
outcome: The emergency pages work with no connectivity, and you know how old the cached guidance is.
prerequisites: One visit to this site with connectivity
completionCriterion: The offline banner shows the snapshot date and the emergency pages open with no network.
recovery: Saving offline changes nothing; it caches public pages only.

steps.title: Save the emergency guide
steps.goal: Cache the emergency bundle.
steps.expected: A confirmation states what was saved and when.
steps.action: Press 'Save emergency guide offline' on the emergency page.
steps.checkpoint: The page shows the documentation snapshot version and cached date.
steps.failure: A cached page without a visible date invites stale guidance to pose as current.

steps.title: Verify it opens with no network
steps.goal: Prove it works before you need it.
steps.expected: The pages open in airplane mode with their offline banner.
steps.action: Disconnect and reload the emergency page.
steps.checkpoint: The offline banner names the snapshot age.
steps.failure: Never test this during an actual emergency. Rehearse now.

title: Recognize fake support and phishing
outcome: You can name the moves impostors use and the rule that defeats all of them.
completionCriterion: You can state the rule: nobody legitimate ever needs your recovery words.

steps.title: Learn the standard moves
steps.goal: Recognize the script.
steps.expected: This page's examples.
steps.action: Read the phishing examples: fake support, urgent upgrades, 'validation' requests, look-alike extensions.
steps.checkpoint: All of them end the same way: they want the words, a signature, or a screen share.
steps.failure: Urgency is the tell. Real infrastructure problems are announced calmly, not delivered as urgent private messages.

steps.title: Hold the one rule
steps.goal: One sentence beats every script.
steps.expected: Certainty.
steps.action: Say it out loud: nobody legitimate ever needs my recovery words, my seed, my screen, or a 'test' signature.
steps.checkpoint: You would refuse a support agent asking for any of those, regardless of urgency or authority.
steps.failure: Every exception you allow becomes the scam that works on you.
